# SemanticOps: terms

### Terms of service

The terms for using the SemanticOps services: free and as is, your content stays yours, and what is not allowed. In force from 5 November 2026.


### These terms

These terms are between you and The-Organization.com Ltd, and by using the services you accept them.

They cover semanticops.com, the editor at app.semanticops.com, essay.semanticops.com and app.mudemocracy.org, and the relay at relay.semanticops.com. Questions: contact@the-organization.com. The [privacy policy](/privacy) explains how data is handled.

The-Organization.com Ltd is registered in England and Wales, company number 10684651. Registered office: 646 Commercial Road, London, England, E14 7HA.


### Free, as is

The services are free for now, with no warranty and no guaranteed availability. They may change or stop.

The relay may become a paid service. People who hold a key will be told before that happens.


### Your content is yours

We claim no rights over your documents or messages, and you are responsible for what you and your guests create and send.

The same goes for what an AI agent you connect writes into your documents, and for what you do with an account at GitHub, Dropbox, Google or an agent's provider, under that company's terms.

SemanticOps software is open source under its own licences, which these terms do not change.


### Keys and links are credentials

Keep your keys, connector links and room links private. Anyone holding a room link can read and post in that room.


### Acceptable use

No unlawful content, no abuse of other people or of the services, and no attempts to get around limits or access controls.

We may revoke a key or block access at any time, for example after misuse.


### Our liability

Keep your own copies of anything that matters. The editor's recovery copy is a convenience, not a backup.

As far as the law allows, we are not liable for lost data or for indirect or consequential loss. Nothing in these terms limits a liability the law does not allow us to limit, or your rights as a consumer.


### Governing law

These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales, and its courts have jurisdiction.

If you use the services as a consumer, you keep the mandatory protections of the country where you live, and you can bring a claim in its courts.


### Changes to these terms

We publish changes on this page with a new date, and using the services afterwards means you accept them.

We email people who hold a peer link key about changes that matter to them.
